designDecisions.decision: Half (i) accepts a SET of declared tokens -- record_retired (new) and not_baked (legacy) -- rather than replacing not_baked, and the set is named in one place (DECLINE_REFUSAL_ERRORS) that the drift control reads.
designDecisions.why: Dispatch item 1 permits keeping not_baked only on evidence that a serving revision still emits it. Both halves of that evidence exist: (a) SOURCE -- the LDT file at 9ce30b81, the commit the production revision was built from, declares both tokens; (b) LIVE -- a probe today against the same route with a fabricated node (48209:999999) answers {"error":"not_baked","errorClass":"no_coverage"}, so the token is not dead code on the deployed surface. Deleting it would have been a change made on a hypothesis the served surface contradicts.
designDecisions.alternativeRejected: Replacing not_baked outright. Rejected: it removes the walk's ability to read an older serving revision (a rollback, or the staging base still pinned pre-P-206), which is precisely the state the 09-14 precedent (A-175) documents.

designDecisions.decision: `isTypedNoCoverageRefusal(res, body)` stays as a boolean wrapper; a new exported `typedNoCoverageRefusalError(res, body)` returns the token that matched, or null.
designDecisions.why: The boolean's existing callers and tests keep their contract, and the walk gains the ability to RECORD which token it saw instead of collapsing two distinct declarations into one boolean. The walk body therefore reports `declinedRetirement.byRefusalError: {record_retired: n, not_baked: n}`, which is what makes a rollback or an out-of-band body visible in the walk's own output rather than silent -- the detection channel the drift control's header names.

designDecisions.decision: The grade still requires BOTH halves, and the reason names both sources; the body's own `retirement` object is recorded (`declinedRefusalCarriedRetirement`) but never graded on.
designDecisions.why: Dispatch item 1, second half. Since P-206 the refusal body may carry a `retirement` object of its own -- the SERVE's assertion about the very node being graded. Accepting on it alone would be accepting the graded artifact's own claim. Half (ii) reads the row from the serving store by a different principal, through the shared predicate, and that independence is the whole reason BOTH-BAKED-HONEST-01 holds.

designDecisions.decision: The drift control compares the walk's DECLINE_REFUSAL_ERRORS against the gtmErrorBody("no_coverage", X) call sites in LDT's brokerageNodeFacets.ts, read from the sparse LDT main checkout the CI workflow already makes, and runs its own self-test first.
designDecisions.why: Dispatch item 3's suggested shape, chosen because the repo already has two guards of exactly this form (check-ldt-vintage-drift.mjs, check-ldt-parcel-table-drift.mjs) reading the same checkout; reusing the checkout costs one sparse-checkout line. Both directions fail: a token the serve declares but the walk does not read (the P-301 defect itself) and a token the walk reads but the serve no longer declares (a dead alternative). The self-test carries the pre-P-206 route as a fixture, so a guard observed only passing is impossible.
designDecisions.statedLimit: It tracks LDT main, not cloudbuild.publish.yaml's _LDT_SHA pin, for the reason the script's header gives: a pin bump lands a whole LDT tree at once, so tracking main makes divergence visible BEFORE the pin moves. The limit, said out loud: what the walk actually reads is a DEPLOYED revision, which lags main; an out-of-band body that never touched main would not be caught here. That is exactly why the walk records byRefusalError.

designDecisions.decision: Item 4's measurement is reported, NOT fixed: the sweep's identity basis and the landing_cad_property vintage split are named as P-178's question.
designDecisions.why: The dispatch's own words -- 'Report, do not fix'. The measurement is in its own artifact; the close states the consequence for this lane (the 16 failures are exactly the account-keyed population) and the consequence it does not settle (whether a passing id is the parcel the sweep believes it is walking).

knownTrapsIAmReadingCarefully: A green local suite is not available on this host: two tests fail on Windows independently of this lane (ctx-b3-store-census.test.mjs:137 reads the LOCAL LDT checkout's leaf set; p3-absence.test.mjs:582 is the documented OPS-21 S3 non-vacuity finding). Both fail identically on origin/main, so the lane's evidence is the DELTA (base 1664 tests/1626 pass/1 fail -> branch 1679 tests/1641 pass/1 fail) plus the Linux CI run, not a Windows green.

The store read is a second principal reading the same store the serve reads. If the bake writes the retirement row and the serve declines BEFORE the row lands, the walk grades BP-MEANING-01 for a legitimate reason; the walk's own storeErrors and byRefusalError counters, plus the row timestamps, are what separate the two cases (on this run the rows predate the walk by ~30 minutes).

The sweep's gold and neighbours come from landing_cad_property, the ACCOUNT namespace, while node ids are parcel-map prop_ids. A passing walk row is a map parcel; whether it is the parcel the sweep meant is a different question (measured: 2 of 3 sampled passing swept ids serve an address that contradicts the swept row) and is reported, not fixed.
